How, precisely, does giving them ZEC make them more likely to use it?

As per this analysis of over 2 million wallets which received free money via airdrops during protocol launches:

https://6thman.ventures/writing/airdrops-analysis.html

Only about 5% to 25% became lifetime unique active wallets, and that's when the money was explicitly meant to get them to use the wallet.

Now you're paying them just to do a job or to fulfill a purpose (like an abortion) entirely unrelated to ZEC, **what** incentivises them to actually learn it? They aren't even curious about it. It's free money.

But then again, it's coinholder decision, so if they want it, it absolutely should pass.

You know me and that I would never go against someone solely because they are trans. And you know that my post has nothing to do with it either.

Further, the ZIP itself says some of these examples are intentionally provocative. That’s my concern in a sentence. The dev fund depends on continued support from coinholders who hold a wide range of views, and deliberately provoking part of that base puts the fund itself at risk, which hurts every project it supports, including the ones this ZIP is meant to help. If the goal is to show that Zcash is for everyone, the examples should make that case without being designed to alienate a share of the people paying for it.

It's not "free money," it's money that is demonstrably different than their existing money. It is money that works around censorship, that is seen (by the person receiving it and would otherwise not be able to receive or spend it) to have capabilities fiat money does not have. Demonstrating these differences in the real world is the only way to convince people who do not already have it that it works the way people they do not trust claim that it does.

The ZECsy program does exactly that, and we have a well-documented track record of showing that this is true. Objections have not been substantive.

If you were at the Zcon7 panel I spoke on, you heard Evan Greer explain why abortion access is difficult to obtain with only surveillable money. She outlined a good use case for shielded ZEC in that example. But it was just an example. I am living proof of another.

That these are not your use cases or that they make some people uncomfortable is not evidence of a lack of utility.

The study you cited polls crypto people. Those people do not have the use cases I do. That is why I use shielded ZEC and transact in shielded ZEC more than the people who just hodl. Showing more people that this can be done and that there are funds ready to demonstrate that utility in their own lives so that they do in fact adopt this capability of money as part of their routine, daily, economic activity is the entire point of the ZIP.

That is what I have proved is possible. That you don't believe me is merely a result of your lack of familiarity with my use case. I am happy to discuss it in more detail should you decide I'm worth buying a drink for next time we have the opportunity to meet at a bar. 🍻

A sex worker, what does she do with the ZEC she receives? Can you guarantee the money is exclusively spent on things that are bought with ZEC, and never swapped for fiat?

I would like for you to answer the above too. Developers aren't taking ZEC, they are taking money, and ZEC is the **only available form** allowed to be paid out by @FPF, as they have repeatedly affirm. We also almost immediately convert it to fiat to fund operations.

Developers never claim they are taking funds because they want to hold ZEC. The mandate is to fund operations, and ZEC being a payout method for that that bears the least hassle. In fact, @ZCG has done fiat grants, and maintains a $6-10M fiat reserve in USD too.

TL;DR For your argument to hold water, can you guarantee that every transaction will be done shielded? Or will it just be converted to fiat to pay rent? If so, why don't we just remove the shielded ZEC part and just say "handing out cryptocurrency so they can be converted to fiat"?

The original argument held water when they were funded to use ZEC in cases where they were legitimately unbanked such that their payments wouldn't blocked. ZCG itself funding them is not such a case.
